answer: In the 2019 first-party account, Wedge was a component-coupling feedback mechanism that surfaced cross-component dependencies by combining runtime Ruby traces with static framework structure such as ActiveRecord associations. It observed runtime cross-component calls, ActiveRecord associations, inheritance and public-API violations and summarized them into an isolation score. The book's case page records the limitation that instrumented execution covers only exercised paths, so dynamic calls and long-term ownership remain hard, which is why the 2020 follow-up built Packwerk around static Ruby constant references checked in pull requests.
